evals.prompt: Users say the export button sometimes does nothing. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Does not jump to a speculative fix. First works to reproduce the intermittent behavior (asks for/derives exact steps, inputs, environment, browser console/network, and what 'sometimes' correlates with), then isolates and forms a root-cause hypothesis, verifies it, fixes the cause, and adds a regression test. Treats 'sometimes' as a signal of nondeterminism to pin down.
assertions: Seeks a reliable reproduction (exact steps/inputs/conditions) before proposing a fix
Treats the intermittency as something to pin down (state/timing/error), not ignore
Forms and verifies a root-cause hypothesis before fixing
Plans a regression test / way to confirm the fix

evals.prompt: This throws "TypeError: cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')" at:  return user.id;  Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Does not merely slap on optional chaining (user?.id) as a symptom patch. Asks/investigates WHY user is undefined at that point (fetch not awaited, lookup returned nothing, auth/session missing, wrong branch) — the root cause — then fixes that cause and adds a test. If a guard is appropriate it is a deliberate, explained choice, not a reflex.
assertions: Investigates WHY user is undefined (root cause) rather than only adding a null guard
Distinguishes fixing the cause from masking the symptom (user?.id)
Proposes verifying the cause and adding regression coverage

evals.prompt: The app crashed on checkout so I wrapped the whole handler in a try/catch and now it doesn't crash. Good enough?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: the try/catch masks the symptom (the crash) while the root cause remains and errors are now swallowed, hiding future bugs and likely leaving checkout broken. Recommends removing/narrowing the catch, reproducing the original crash, finding and verifying the real cause, fixing that, and only then handling errors intentionally.
assertions: Identifies that the try/catch masks the symptom without fixing the root cause
Warns that swallowing the error hides the real bug (checkout may still be broken)
Recommends reproducing and finding/verifying the actual cause before considering it fixed

evals.prompt: This test passes sometimes and fails other times. Just make it pass.
evals.expected_output: Does not blindly rerun, add sleeps, or retry to force a pass. Investigates the source of nondeterminism (shared/leaking state, test ordering, real clock/network/random, async timing) via isolation, then fixes the determinism (inject clock/seed, control ordering, reset state) rather than masking it. Notes that a flaky test hidden, not fixed, will recur.
assertions: Does NOT just rerun/retry or add arbitrary sleeps to force a pass
Investigates the source of nondeterminism (shared state, ordering, timing, clock/random)
Fixes the determinism / root cause rather than masking the flakiness
